definitions.explanation: a horticultural technique where a cutting from one plant (scion) is inserted into another plant (rootstock) so they grow together as one

examples.japanese: ⟦{果樹|かじゅ}→果樹：27144_kaju⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{接|つ}ぎ{木|き}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{増|ふ}やす→増やす：02410_fuyasu⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: Fruit trees are often propagated by grafting.

examples.japanese: {接|つ}ぎ{木|き}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{病気|びょうき}→病気：00771_byouki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{強|つよ}い→強い：00820_tsuyoi⟧⟦{木|き}→木：00524_ki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{作|つく}れる→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: By grafting, you can create trees that are resistant to disease.

examples.japanese: {接|つ}ぎ{木|き}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{技術|ぎじゅつ}→技術：01389_gijutsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{古代|こだい}→古代：05324_kodai⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{使|つか}われて→使う：00473_tsukau⟧きた。
examples.english: Grafting techniques have been used since ancient times.

notes:
USAGE:
{接|つ}ぎ{木|き} is essential in fruit tree cultivation, allowing farmers to combine desired fruit characteristics (scion) with a hardy root system (rootstock). Can also be used as a verb: {接|つ}ぎ{木|き}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧.

ADVANTAGES OF GRAFTING:
- Combines disease-resistant rootstocks with high-quality fruit varieties
- Produces fruit faster than growing from seed
- Maintains exact genetic characteristics of the parent plant

RELATED WORDS:
- {台木|だいぎ} (rootstock)
- {穂木|ほぎ} (scion)
- ⟦{挿|さ}し{木|き}→挿し木：08105_sashiki⟧ (cutting propagation)
